subject: Scheduling: Dedicated capacity sizing call (FintechCo) - next steps
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Intro + discovery follow-up: Redwood inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Good overview of Redwood’s Dedicated offering and the routing/cache options. We’re excited about the possibility of moving to a reserved capacity setup to meet our real-time scoring needs.

Quick recap from our side:
- Primary use case: real-time risk scoring for transactions (text + small structured metadata)
- Desired 99th pct latency: ~200ms (ideally <150ms) for single-request scoring
- Typical payload: ~1–2 KB per request; peak QPS expected around 250, sustained ~80–120 QPS
- Batchability: low — most requests need immediate responses

Can we schedule the dedicated capacity sizing call (tech/deep-dive) next week so your SRE/solutions engineer can run through throughput/latency sizing? We’re available: Mon 28 Jun 10:00–11:00 PT, Tue 29 Jun 13:00–14:00 PT, Wed 30 Jun 09:00–10:00 PT.

Also, happy to share anonymized logs and a small sample of payloads ahead of time if that helps.

Thanks —
Alex

Hi Alex —

Really appreciate the clear recap. That latency/QPS profile is helpful and exactly the kind of context we need.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Schedule a 60-minute Dedicated capacity sizing call with our solutions engineer (David Kim) to size GPU pools, discuss autoscale/burst, and validate tail latency targets.
2) You send the anonymized logs + 24h spike sample and a few representative payloads (we’ll use them to estimate batching and KV-cache effects).
3) We’ll share a short pre-call workbook and our preliminary capacity proposal (attached).

Proposed slots based on your availability:
- Mon, 28 Jun, 10:00–11:00 PT (preferred)
- Tue, 29 Jun, 13:00–14:00 PT
- Wed, 30 Jun, 09:00–10:00 PT

I’ve attached our preliminary proposal for dedicated capacity so you have context before the call (redwood-dedicated-capacity-proposal.pdf). David — added you here to pick the final slot and call agenda.

Thanks,

—

Subject: RE: Scheduling: Dedicated capacity sizing call (FintechCo) - next steps

Hi Alex / Marissa —

I’m David (solutions engineer) — happy to lead the sizing session. Thanks for the notes; to make the call most effective, can you confirm/provide the following before we meet?
- Peak and sustained QPS across your busiest 24h window (you listed peak ~250 QPS — please confirm).
- 95th and 99th percentile latency measured today (if available) and whether that includes network time.
- Average prompt length (tokens/characters) and whether you use streaming responses or full payload returns.
- Typical concurrency pattern (many short bursts vs steady state).
- A representative sample of requests (10–20) and a 1–2 hour log snippet showing spikes.

I’ve uploaded a short sizing workbook and a configuration template for Nimbus (nimbus-configuration.xlsx) — filling the workbook helps us give an initial GPU-pool recommendation during the call. Also included is a short pre-call agenda:
- 10m: goals & current architecture
- 25m: traffic/payload deep-dive and logs walkthrough
- 20m: sizing recommendations & tradeoffs (batching, quantization, cache profiles)
- 5m: next steps/POC timeline

If Mon 28 10:00 PT works, I’ll send a calendar invite for a 60-minute slot and include a Google Meet link. Otherwise, Tue 29 13:00 PT works for me as well.

Attachment: nimbus-configuration.xlsx (Excel, 46 KB)

Thanks — looking forward to it.

-David
David Kim
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Please send the calendar invite when you can. Looking forward to the call.
